issues.legal_issue: A change in the identity of contracted land resulting from completed consolidation proceedings does not bar specific performance where substantially the same land is allotted and the purchaser relinquishes a minor shortfall.
material_facts: The owner agreed to sell a share in agricultural land, and the purchaser sued to enforce the agreement after the owner had died.
The suit was filed after consolidation proceedings had concluded.
The consolidation allotment included substantially the same land covered by the agreement, except for a small portion that was due to the purchaser and that the purchaser gave up.
The specific-performance decree was challenged on the ground that consolidation had caused the land to lose its identity.
issues.conclusion: The changed identity of the land did not prevent specific performance. Section 12(2) of the Specific Relief Act covered the situation, and, because the consolidation proceedings had concluded, there was no bar to enforcing the agreement. The appeal was dismissed subject to the parties' agreed modifications to the decree.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(2) of the Specific Relief Act covers the situation where consolidation has altered the land but substantially the same land is allotted and the purchaser gives up a small shortfall; once consolidation proceedings have concluded, they do not bar specific performance. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

rule.if: specific_performance_appeal and consolidation_completed and substantially_same_land_allotted and purchaser_relinquished_shortfall

predicates.specific_performance_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a decree enforcing a contract to sell land.
predicates.consolidation_completed: The land-consolidation proceedings had concluded before the suit seeking enforcement was filed.
predicates.substantially_same_land_allotted: The consolidation allotment included substantially the same land as the land covered by the sale agreement.
predicates.purchaser_relinquished_shortfall: The purchaser gave up a small portion that was due to the purchaser but was not included in the allotment.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges specific performance of a land-sale agreement, consolidation has concluded, substantially the contracted land has been allotted, and the purchaser has relinquished a small shortfall, the contract is enforceable by specific performance.
